title: LEASES RESTRICTIONS ACT 1976
text:
LEASES RESTRICTIONS ACT 1976 

 LEASES RESTRICTIONS ACT 1976 

 1  

 Short title 

 This Act may be cited as the Leases Restrictions Act 1976.

LEASES RESTRICTIONS ACT 1976 

 LEASES RESTRICTIONS ACT 1976 

 2  

 Interpretation 

 In this Act unless the content requires otherwise— 

 assignment of lease 

 includes any assignment, transfer, or conveyance of a lease or a sublease 

 lease 

 includes any agreement to lease but does not include any lease under the Short Term Crop Leases Act 1966 or any lease for a term not exceeding 5 years (inclusive of any right of renewal) 

 Minister 

 means the Minister of Justice 

 sublease 

 includes any agreement to sublease but does not include any sublease for a term not exceeding 5 years (inclusive of any right of renewal) 

 Tribunal 

 means the Leases Approval Tribunal established under section 4 and continued in force under that section (as replaced by section 5 of the Leases Restrictions Amendment Act 2020). 

 [Section 2 Tribunal: replaced, on 30 June 2020, by section 4 of the Leases Restrictions Amendment Act 2020 (2020 No 12) .] 

 [Section 2 Minister: inserted, on 13 November 2005, by section 2 of the Leases Restrictions Amendment Act 2005 (2005 No 16) .]

LEASES RESTRICTIONS ACT 1976 

 LEASES RESTRICTIONS ACT 1976 

 3  

 Approval of Leases Approval Tribunal required 

 (1)  

 Despite any other provision in any Act, no lease, assignment of lease, or sublease executed after the coming into force of this Act is valid and of any effect unless the approval of the Tribunal has been obtained to that lease, assignment of lease, or sublease, as the case may be. 

 (2)  

 The Tribunal must approve any lease, assignment of lease or sublease to give effect to any order made by the High Court or Court of Appeal pursuant to this or any other Act. 

 (3)  

 Despite any provision in the Cook Islands Act 1915, no lease, assignment of lease, or sublease may be confirmed by the High Court unless the approval of the Tribunal to the lease, assignment of lease or sublease has been first obtained. 

 (4)  

 Despite any provision in the Land (Facilitation of Dealings) Act 1970, no resolution of any meeting of assembled owners to lease any land may be confirmed by the High Court unless the approval of the Tribunal has been first obtained. 

 [Section 3: replaced, on 9 May 2002, by section 3 of the Leases Restrictions Amendment Act 2002 (2002 No 5) .]

LEASES RESTRICTIONS ACT 1976 

 LEASES RESTRICTIONS ACT 1976 

 4  

 Leases Approval Tribunal 

 (1)  

 There continues to be a Leases Approval Tribunal of not less than 2 nor more than 5 members all of whom must be appointed for a term of 3 years by the Minister with the concurrence of Cabinet. 

 (2)  

 A member of the Tribunal may at any time— 

 (a) 

 be removed from office by the Minister for disability, bankruptcy, neglect of duty, or misconduct, proved to the satisfaction of the Minister; or 

 (b) 

 resign by notice in writing addressed to the Minister. 

 (3)  

 Despite subsection (1), every member of the Tribunal, unless that member sooner vacates office under subsection (2), continues in office until— 

 (a) 

 that member’s successor comes into office; or 

 (b) 

 the Secretary for Justice notifies that member that no successor to that member is to be appointed. 

 (4)  

 The Leases Approval Tribunal referred to in subsection (1) is the same body as the Leases Approval Tribunal in existence before the commencement of section 5 of the Leases Restrictions Amendment Act 2020. 

 [Section 4: replaced, on 30 June 2020, by section 5 of the Leases Restrictions Amendment Act 2020 (2020 No 12) .]

LEASES RESTRICTIONS ACT 1976 

 LEASES RESTRICTIONS ACT 1976 

 5  

 Functions of Leases Approval Tribunal 

 The functions of the Tribunal are: 

 (a) 

 to consider applications for approval of leases, assignments of leases, and subleases and to grant its approval in any case where it is satisfied that the criteria set out in the regulations pursuant to section 13 for such approvals have been satisfied or met: 

 (b) 

 to consider applications for approval upon criteria set out in the regulations pursuant to section 13— 

 (i) 

 prior to the confirmation of a unit plan pursuant to section 5(d) of the Unit Titles Act 2005; or 

 (ii) 

 prior to an assignment, sublease, dealing, or transfer of or additions to common property pursuant to sections 10(3), 18, 19(2)(b), and 20(1) and (2) of the Unit Titles Act 2005; or 

 (iii) 

 prior to a dealing in a stratum estate in leasehold pursuant to section 25 of the Unit Titles Act 2005; or 

 (iv) 

 prior to the confirmation of a redevelopment plan pursuant to section 46(6)(d) of the Unit Titles Act 2005; or 

 (v) 

 prior to the cancellation of a unit plan pursuant to section 47(3)(d) of the Unit Titles Act 2005; or 

 (vi) 

 prior to the settlement of a scheme following destruction or damage pursuant to section 48(1) of the Unit Titles Act 2005; or 

 (vii) 

 where there is a dealing with an accessory unit or an interest in an accessory unit which includes a principal unit or a corresponding interest in a principal unit pursuant to section 11(2) of the Unit Titles Act 2005: 

 (c) 

 to make recommendations from time to time to the Minister with regard to the criteria to be applied in granting approvals to leases, assignments of leases and subleases: 

 (d) 

 to report to the Minister from time to time and when required to do so by the Minister on matters relating to leases, assignments of leases, subleases generally and to dealings pursuant to the Unit Titles Act 2005. 

 [Section 5: replaced, on 13 November 2005, by section 3 of the Leases Restrictions Amendment Act 2005 (2005 No 16) .]

LEASES RESTRICTIONS ACT 1976 

 LEASES RESTRICTIONS ACT 1976 

 6  

 Policy Directives to Tribunal [Repealed] 

 [Repealed] 

 [Section 6: repealed, on 13 November 2005, by section 4 of the Leases Restrictions Amendment Act 2005 (2005 No 16) .]

LEASES RESTRICTIONS ACT 1976 

 LEASES RESTRICTIONS ACT 1976 

 7  

 Duties of Leases Approval Tribunal 

 The Leases Approval Tribunal must perform its functions under this Act diligently and with due regard to the need to determine applications in a prompt and efficient manner. 

 [Section 7 heading: amended, on 9 May 2002, by section 4(2) of the Leases Restrictions Amendment Act 2002 (2002 No 5) .] 

 [Section 7: amended, on 9 May 2002, by section 4(2) of the Leases Restrictions Amendment Act 2002 (2002 No 5) .]

LEASES RESTRICTIONS ACT 1976 

 LEASES RESTRICTIONS ACT 1976 

 8  

 Procedure of Leases Approval Tribunal 

 (1)  

 Subject to the provisions of this Act and any regulations made hereunder the Leases Approval Tribunal may regulate its own procedure. 

 (2)  

 The Department of Justice must provide the Leases Approval Tribunal with such secretarial and clerical services as the Tribunal may require. 

 (3)  

 The Chairperson must be appointed by the Minister responsible for Justice with the concurrence of Cabinet. 

 (4)  

 Meetings of the Leases Approval Tribunal must be called by reasonable notice to all members of the Tribunal present in Rarotonga, and must be held at such times and places as the Chairperson or in his or her absence the Deputy Chairperson determines. 

 (5)  

 Any party interested in an application before the Tribunal is entitled to appear before the Tribunal personally or through his or her solicitor or agent for the purposes of making representations or giving information to the Tribunal. 

 (6)  

 The quorum for meetings of the Tribunal shall be established by the Tribunal from time to time. 

 (7)  

 Any decision or determination by the Tribunal must be made by a majority vote of the members present at the meeting. 

 [Section 8 heading: amended, on 9 May 2002, by section 4(2) of the Leases Restrictions Amendment Act 2002 (2002 No 5) .] 

 [Section 8: amended, on 9 May 2002, by section 4(2) of the Leases Restrictions Amendment Act 2002 (2002 No 5) .]

LEASES RESTRICTIONS ACT 1976 

 LEASES RESTRICTIONS ACT 1976 

 9  

 Application for approval 

 Every application for approval of the Leases Approval Tribunal must be made in writing in the form or to the effect of the form prescribed by the Tribunal from time to time and must be accompanied by a fee as may from time to time be prescribed in the regulations. 

 [Section 9: amended, on 9 May 2002, by section 4(2) of the Leases Restrictions Amendment Act 2002 (2002 No 5) .]

LEASES RESTRICTIONS ACT 1976 

 LEASES RESTRICTIONS ACT 1976 

 9A  

 Leases not executed by all parties 

 (1)  

 The Tribunal may consider an application to approve a lease that has not been executed by every party to the lease only if the Registrar of the High Court notifies the Tribunal in writing that he or she believes that the lease should be approved. 

 (2)  

 In determining whether to make the notification, the Registrar of the High Court must apply the criteria and other matters referred to in section 11. 

 [Section 9A: inserted, on 9 May 2002, by section 6 of the Leases Restrictions Amendment Act 2002 (2002 No 5) .]

LEASES RESTRICTIONS ACT 1976 

 LEASES RESTRICTIONS ACT 1976 

 10  

 Further information 

 (1)  

 In the event that the Leases Approval Tribunal considers that insufficient information has been made available to it in application or supporting documents to that application the Tribunal may require the applicant to supply such further information as it considers relevant to the criteria to be applied by the Tribunal and must defer consideration of the application until that further information is supplied. 

 (2)  

 In the event of any dispute or issue arising from any application before it, the Tribunal may, upon such terms and conditions it deems necessary, direct that a meeting of the landowners be held to resolve the dispute or issue. 

 [Section 10(1): amended, on 9 May 2002, by sections 4(2), 7(a) and 7(b) of the Leases Restrictions Amendment Act 2002 (2002 No 5) .] 

 [Section 10(2): inserted, on 9 May 2002, by section 7(b) of the Leases Restrictions Amendment Act 2002 (2002 No 5) .]

LEASES RESTRICTIONS ACT 1976 

 LEASES RESTRICTIONS ACT 1976 

 11  

 Criteria to be applied by Tribunal 

 In considering any application before it, the Leases Approval Tribunal must apply the criteria prescribed in regulations made pursuant to section 13. 

 [Section 11: replaced, on 13 November 2005, by section 5 of the Leases Restrictions Amendment Act 2005 (2005 No 16) .]

LEASES RESTRICTIONS ACT 1976 

 LEASES RESTRICTIONS ACT 1976 

 12  

 False information 

 Any person who knowingly supplies any false information to the Leases Approval Tribunal which is material to any application commits an offence and is liable upon conviction to a fine not exceeding $200 or to imprisonment for a term not exceeding 3 months or both. 

 [Section 12: amended, on 9 May 2002, by section 4(2) of the Leases Restrictions Amendment Act 2002 (2002 No 5) .]

LEASES RESTRICTIONS ACT 1976 

 LEASES RESTRICTIONS ACT 1976 

 13  

 Regulations 

 (1)  

 The Queen’s Representative may from time to time, by Order in Executive Council, make all such regulations as may, in his or her opinion, be deemed necessary or expedient for giving full effect to the provisions of this Act and for the due administration hereof. 

 (2)  

 All regulations made under this section must be laid before Parliament within 28 days after the date of their making if Parliament is then in session, and, if not, must be laid before Parliament within 28 days after the date of the commencement of the next ensuing session. 

 [Section 13(1): amended, on 6 April 1982, by section 4(3) of the Constitution Amendment (No 10) Act 1981-82 (1981-82 No 20) .]

LEASES RESTRICTIONS ACT 1976 

 LEASES RESTRICTIONS ACT 1976 

 14  

 Effect of Development Investment Act 1995-96 

 Nothing in the Development Investment Act 1995-96 affects this Act. 

 [Section 14: inserted, on 9 May 2002, by section 9 of the Leases Restrictions Amendment Act 2002 (2002 No 5) .]

LEASES RESTRICTIONS ACT 1976 

 LEASES RESTRICTIONS ACT 1976 

 15  

 Effect of Unit Titles Act 2005 

 Nothing in the Unit Titles Act 2005 affects this Act. 

 [Section 15: inserted, on 13 November 2005, by section 6 of the Leases Restrictions Amendment Act 2005 (2005 No 16) .]

LEASES RESTRICTIONS ACT 1976 

 LEASES RESTRICTIONS ACT 1976 

 16  

 Validation 

 Anything purportedly done by or in relation to the Leases Approval Tribunal ( Tribunal ) on or after 15 January 2011 and before 6 December 2011 is not invalid, and is taken never to have been invalid, merely because of either or both of the following: 

 (a) 

 there was a defect or irregularity of any kind in connection with the appointment of 1 or more, or all, members of the Tribunal: 

 (b) 

 the appointment of 1 or more, or all, members of the Tribunal had ceased to have effect for any reason. 

 [Section 16: inserted, on 13 December 2011, by section 3 of the Leases Restrictions Amendment Act 2011 (2011 No 13) .]

LEASES RESTRICTIONS ACT 1976 

 LEASES RESTRICTIONS ACT 1976 

 17  

 Further validation 

 Anything done or purportedly done by or in relation to the Tribunal on or after 20 November 2017 and before 15 October 2019 is not invalid, and has never been invalid because of either or both of the following: 

 (a) 

 a defect or irregularity of any kind in connection with the appointment of 1 or more, or all, members of the Tribunal: 

 (b) 

 the appointment of 1 or more, or all, members of the Tribunal ceasing to have effect for any reason. 

 [Section 17: inserted, on 30 June 2020, by section 6 of the Leases Restrictions Amendment Act 2020 (2020 No 12) .]

LEASES RESTRICTIONS REGULATIONS 1977 

 LEASES RESTRICTIONS REGULATIONS 1977 

 1  

 Short title and commencement 

 (1)  

 These regulations may be cited as the Leases Restrictions Regulations 1977. 

 (2)  

 These regulations come into force on 18 May 1977.

LEASES RESTRICTIONS REGULATIONS 1977 

 LEASES RESTRICTIONS REGULATIONS 1977 

 2  

 Interpretation 

 In these regulations unless the context otherwise requires— 

 Act 

 means the Leases Restrictions Act 1976 

 applicant 

 means any person who has made application to the Committee 

 Chairperson 

 means the person appointed as Chairperson of the Committee 

 Committee 

 means the Leases Approval Committee 

 Secretary 

 means the Secretary to the Committee.

LEASES RESTRICTIONS REGULATIONS 1977 

 PART 1  PROCEDURE 

 3  

 Procedure and practice 

 (1)  

 Subject to the provisions of these regulations, no practice which is inconsistent with these regulations may prevail in any sitting of the Committee. 

 (2)  

 If any case arises for which no form of procedure has been provided by the Act or these regulations, the Committee must dispose of the case in such manner as the Committee deems best calculated to deal with the case. 

 (3)  

 The Committee may from time to time as it considers necessary make such rules not inconsistent with the Act or these regulations for regulating the conduct of its business.

LEASES RESTRICTIONS REGULATIONS 1977 

 PART 1  PROCEDURE 

 4  

 Failure to comply with these regulations 

 Failure to comply with any of these regulations does not render any proceedings of the Committee void unless expressly so provided for in the Act or unless the Committee so directs: 
 Provided that any such proceedings may be set aside either wholly or in part as irregular or may be amended or otherwise dealt with in such manner and upon such terms as the Committee thinks fit.

LEASES RESTRICTIONS REGULATIONS 1977 

 PART 1  PROCEDURE 

 5  

 Forms 

 The forms prescribed by these regulations for use in any proceedings before the Committee are those set forth in Schedule 1: 
 Provided that such forms may be used with such modifications as the case may require and if no form is prescribed by these regulations, then such form may be used as the Committee may direct or approve.

LEASES RESTRICTIONS REGULATIONS 1977 

 PART 1  PROCEDURE 

 6  

 Sittings of Committee 

 (1)  

 The Committee must sit at such times and at such places as the Chairperson may from time to time appoint. 

 (2)  

 The time and place appointed for the sitting of the Committee must be publicly notified in such manner as the Committee directs.

LEASES RESTRICTIONS REGULATIONS 1977 

 PART 1  PROCEDURE 

 7  

 Applications to be notified 

 The Secretary must at least 7 clear days before the sitting of the Committee notify the parties to the transaction to be dealt with at the sitting of the Committee.

LEASES RESTRICTIONS REGULATIONS 1977 

 PART 1  PROCEDURE 

 8  

 Commencement of proceedings before Committee 

 (1)  

 Unless otherwise prescribed by the Act or these regulations, every proceedings before the Committee must be commenced by an application in the form LAC 1 in Schedule 1 and filed with the Secretary at Rarotonga. 

 (2)  

 Any application may be filed by delivery through the post and is deemed to have been filed upon receipt thereof by the Secretary and upon payment of the fee prescribed in Schedule 2. 

 (3)  

 Every application must be signed by the applicant or his or her authorised agent and where directed by the Secretary under regulation 9 must be attested. 

 (4)  

 A declaration of compliance in form LAC 3 in Schedule 1 must be filed with every application made to the Committee.

LEASES RESTRICTIONS REGULATIONS 1977 

 PART 1  PROCEDURE 

 9  

 Secretary may require application to be attested 

 The Secretary may if he or she considers necessary require the signature of any applicant to be attested.

LEASES RESTRICTIONS REGULATIONS 1977 

 PART 1  PROCEDURE 

 10  

 Secretary may refuse application 

 Unless directed otherwise by the Committee, the Secretary if in his or her opinion an application is not properly made or is not in conformity with the requirements of the Act or these regulations must refuse to accept the application and must return it to the applicant.

LEASES RESTRICTIONS REGULATIONS 1977 

 PART 1  PROCEDURE 

 11  

 Procedure at hearing 

 (1)  

 The Chairperson must preside at every sitting of the Committee. 

 (2)  

 It is the duty of one of the Committee members to record the proceedings of the Committee in a minute book provided for the purpose which minute book is a record of the proceedings before the Committee and must be retained in the custody or the Secretary. 

 (3)  

 Any person who is affected by any application is entitled to appear and be heard upon the application. 

 (4)  

 The Committee may if it thinks necessary arrange the order in which the parties appearing in respect of any application are heard. 

 (5)  

 The Committee may if it thinks fit, arrange the order of its business and determine the procedure in matters not specifically provided in these regulations.

LEASES RESTRICTIONS REGULATIONS 1977 

 PART 1  PROCEDURE 

 12  

 Committee may require further information 

 (1)  

 The Committee may if it considers necessary require an applicant to produce to the Committee such further documents and other information as are required to dispose or the application. 

 (2)  

 The Committee may decline to deal with an application if the requirements or subclause (1) have not been complied with. 

 (3)  

 The Committee may if it considers necessary call for evidence and advice from professional and technical persons to assist the Committee in its deliberations.

LEASES RESTRICTIONS REGULATIONS 1977 

 PART 1  PROCEDURE 

 13  

 Decision of Committee 

 Every application dealt with by the Committee must be endorsed with the decision of the Committee and must be signed by the Chairperson.

LEASES RESTRICTIONS REGULATIONS 1977 

 PART 1  PROCEDURE 

 14  

 Certificate of Approval 

 The certificate of approval of the Committee must be in form LAC 4 in Schedule 1.

LEASES RESTRICTIONS REGULATIONS 1977 

 PART 1  PROCEDURE 

 15  

 Minute book to be signed by members of Committee 

 The minute book containing the proceedings before the Committee must be signed respectively by each member of the Committee presiding.

LEASES RESTRICTIONS REGULATIONS 1977 

 PART 1  PROCEDURE 

 16  

 Fees 

 The fees set out in Schedule 2 are the fees to be paid in respect of the proceedings of the Committee.

LEASES RESTRICTIONS REGULATIONS 1977 

 PART 2  CRITERIA TO BE APPLIED BY TRIBUNAL 

 17  

 Criteria to be applied by Tribunal 

 (1)  

 Before the Tribunal makes a decision on any application for approval of a lease, sublease, assignment of lease or assignment of sublease it must apply the criteria set out in these regulations. 

 [Regulation 17: inserted, on 14 October 2005, by regulation 5 of the Leases Restrictions (Amendment) Regulations 2006 (SN 2006/2) .]

LEASES RESTRICTIONS REGULATIONS 1977 

 PART 2  CRITERIA TO BE APPLIED BY TRIBUNAL 

 18  

 Restrictions against alienation of land to certain persons 

 [Repealed] 

 [Regulation 18: revoked, on 14 October 2005, by regulation 6 of the Leases Restrictions (Amendment) Regulations 2006 (SN 2006/2) .]

LEASES RESTRICTIONS REGULATIONS 1977 

 PART 2  CRITERIA TO BE APPLIED BY TRIBUNAL 

 19  

 Approval may be given in certain cases 

 The Tribunal may grant approval to any lease or sublease or assignment of lease or assignment of sublease to: 

 (a) 

 any person who is not a Cook Islander if that person is the spouse of a Cook Islander; and 

 (b) 

 the Cook Islander spouse is joint owner in the deed for the transaction sought to be approved by the Tribunal; and 

 (c) 

 express provision is made in the deed document for the transaction that in the event of the Cook Islander spouse predeceasing the non-Cook Islander spouse the approval of the Lessors under the head lease must be obtained for the non-Cook Islander’s interest for the unexpired term of the leasehold interest to continue and where such deceased Cook Islander spouse and such surviving non-Cook Islander spouse have together issue surviving then such issue become co-owners of the leasehold interest with the non-Cook Islander spouse until the expiry of the lease; or 

 (d) 

 any person who is not a Cook Islander if the High Court or Court of Appeal so orders; or 

 (e) 

 any company incorporated or re-registered under the Companies Act 2017 if— 

 (i) 

 not less than 55% of the shareholding in the Company or not less than 51% of the controlling interest in the company is held by one or more Cook Islanders or permanent residents; and 

 (ii) 

 provision is made that no transfer may be made of the local shareholding during the period of 5 years from the date of approval of the Tribunal; and 

 (iii) 

 approval is not being sought for residential purposes; or 

 (f) 

 any enterprise or foreign enterprise registered in the Cook Islands pursuant to the provisions of the Development Investment Act 1995-96 if— 

 (i) 

 a certificate has been issued by the Development Investment Board pursuant to section 19 of the Development Investment Act 1995-96 and given to the Tribunal certifying that the enterprise or foreign enterprise has been registered under that Act; and 

 (ii) 

 provision is made that no transfer may be made of the local shareholding during the period of 5 years from the date of approval of the Tribunal; and 

 (iii) 

 approval is not being sought for residential purposes; or 

 (g) 

 the government of New Zealand and any agency of that government where— 

 (i) 

 Cabinet has approved the use to which the leased land will be put; and 

 (ii) 

 that use is a public purpose within the meaning of section 364 of the Cook Islands Act 1915; and 

 (iii) 

 the occupational use of the lease cannot be varied. 

 [Regulation 19: inserted, on 14 October 2005, by regulation 5 of the Leases Restrictions (Amendment) Regulations 2006 (SN 2006/2) .] 

 [Regulation 19(e): amended, on 10 December 2009, by Schedule 16 clause 14 of the Companies Act 2017 (2017 No 14) .] 

 [Regulation 19(g): inserted, on 2 March 2016, by regulation 4 of the Leases Restrictions Amendment Regulations 2016 (SN 2016/3) .]

LEASES RESTRICTIONS REGULATIONS 1977 

 PART 2  CRITERIA TO BE APPLIED BY TRIBUNAL 

 20  

 Requirement for Certificate of explanation in Cook Islands Maori 

 The Tribunal must not approve any lease or sublease or assignment of lease or assignment of sublease where one of the parties to the transaction is a Cook Islander unless the Tribunal is satisfied that— 

 (a) 

 the nature and extent of the transaction and the implication of the provisions of the deed document for the transaction has been explained to that Cook Islander in the Cook Islands Maori language by an officer of the High Court approved in writing by the Secretary of Justice or the Registrar to be competent for the purpose; and 

 (b) 

 an appropriate certificate duly signed to that effect by the person who carried out the explanation has been endorsed on the document; and 

 (c) 

 the person to whom the explanation in Cook Islands Maori has been given was not held responsible for the cost of providing that explanation but that cost is met by the party or their representative who requires the transaction to be recorded in English, and 

 (d) 

 the alienation complies with the provisions of section 475 of the Cook Islands Act 1915. 

 [Regulation 20: inserted, on 14 October 2005, by regulation 5 of the Leases Restrictions (Amendment) Regulations 2006 (SN 2006/2) .]

LEASES RESTRICTIONS REGULATIONS 1977 

 PART 2  CRITERIA TO BE APPLIED BY TRIBUNAL 

 21  

 Approval dependent upon holding of meeting of assembled owners 

 The Tribunal must not approve any sublease or assignment of lease or assignment of sublease unless it is satisfied upon written evidence being produced by the applicant certifying that a meeting of assembled owners resident on the island on which the land is situated has been held and that the assembled owners have by consensus consented to the transaction. 

 [Regulation 21: inserted, on 14 October 2005, by regulation 5 of the Leases Restrictions (Amendment) Regulations 2006 (SN 2006/2) .]

LEASES RESTRICTIONS REGULATIONS 1977 

 PART 2  CRITERIA TO BE APPLIED BY TRIBUNAL 

 22  

 Application to be reconsidered or adjourned if opposed by owner 

 Where any of the owners in the land concerned opposes the transaction the Tribunal must not approve any lease or sublease or assignment of lease or assignment of sublease except that the Tribunal may— 

 (a) 

 reconsider the application if the Tribunal deems the objection to be valid and reasonable; or 

 (b) 

 adjourn the application upon such conditions as the Tribunal may impose to allow the opposition to the application to be disposed of or settled between the parties. 

 [Regulation 22: inserted, on 14 October 2005, by regulation 5 of the Leases Restrictions (Amendment) Regulations 2006 (SN 2006/2) .]

LEASES RESTRICTIONS REGULATIONS 1977 

 PART 2  CRITERIA TO BE APPLIED BY TRIBUNAL 

 23  

 Alienation complies with Cook Islands Act 1915 

 The Tribunal must not approve any lease, sublease or assignment of lease or assignment of sublease unless the Tribunal is satisfied upon the provision by direction or otherwise of such relevant information as may assist the Tribunal, that— 

 (a) 

 the mode of execution of the instrument of alienation is in conformity with the Cook Islands Act 1915: 

 (b) 

 the alienation is not contrary to equity or good faith or to the interests of the persons alienating or to the public interest. 

 [Regulation 23: inserted, on 14 October 2005, by regulation 5 of the Leases Restrictions (Amendment) Regulations 2006 (SN 2006/2) .]

LEASES RESTRICTIONS REGULATIONS 1977 

 PART 2  CRITERIA TO BE APPLIED BY TRIBUNAL 

 24  

 Monetary consideration, annual rental 

 The Tribunal must not approve any lease, sublease or assignment of lease or assignment of sublease unless the Tribunal is satisfied upon the provision by direction or otherwise of such relevant information as may assist the Tribunal, that— 

 (a) 

 any monetary consideration paid and annual rental payable to the owners in the land is adequate fair and reasonable and complies with section 482 of the Cook Islands Act 1915; or 

 (b) 

 in the case of an enterprise or foreign enterprise the monetary consideration paid and annual rental payable to the owners in the land complies with section 106A of the Property Law Act 1952 as it applies in the Cook Islands. 

 [Regulation 24: inserted, on 14 October 2005, by regulation 5 of the Leases Restrictions (Amendment) Regulations 2006 (SN 2006/2) .]

LEASES RESTRICTIONS REGULATIONS 1977 

 PART 2  CRITERIA TO BE APPLIED BY TRIBUNAL 

 25  

 Owners or Cook Islanders to be given first right of refusal in lease 

 The Tribunal must not approve any sublease or assignment of lease or assignment of sublease unless the deed for the transaction expressly provides for— 

 (a) 

 the owners in the land residing on the island on which the land is situated to be given first notice of any intended assignment or subletting and first option to purchase or refuse to purchase such assignment or subletting and the Tribunal is satisfied that such provision is reasonable; or 

 (b) 

 a Cook Islander residing in the Cook Islands to be given first right of refusal where there are no owners in the land residing on the island on which the land is situated willing to purchase such assignment or subletting and the Tribunal is satisfied that the lessee has made reasonable attempts to give notice of the intended assignment or subletting and the Tribunal is satisfied that such provision is reasonable. 

 [Regulation 25: inserted, on 14 October 2005, by regulation 5 of the Leases Restrictions (Amendment) Regulations 2006 (SN 2006/2) .]

LEASES RESTRICTIONS REGULATIONS 1977 

 PART 2  CRITERIA TO BE APPLIED BY TRIBUNAL 

 26  

 Specific purposes to be stated in lease 

 The Tribunal must not approve any lease, sublease or assignment of lease or assignment of sublease unless the purpose for the lease, sublease, assignment of lease or assignment of sublease is explicitly stated in the deed of lease and the Tribunal must refuse approval if the purpose is vague or too general or is not specific. 

 [Regulation 26: inserted, on 14 October 2005, by regulation 5 of the Leases Restrictions (Amendment) Regulations 2006 (SN 2006/2) .]

LEASES RESTRICTIONS REGULATIONS 1977 

 PART 2  CRITERIA TO BE APPLIED BY TRIBUNAL 

 27  

 Approval to be refused if land required for family needs 

 The Tribunal must not approve any lease, sublease or assignment of lease or assignment of sublease if the Tribunal is satisfied upon the provision by direction or otherwise of such relevant information as may assist the Tribunal, that within 5 years of the date of application the land would be required for the needs of the owners in the land and their families. 

 [Regulation 27: inserted, on 14 October 2005, by regulation 5 of the Leases Restrictions (Amendment) Regulations 2006 (SN 2006/2) .]

LEASES RESTRICTIONS REGULATIONS 1977 

 PART 2  CRITERIA TO BE APPLIED BY TRIBUNAL 

 28  

 Breach of condition in head lease may bar approval 

 The Tribunal must not approve any lease, sublease or assignment of lease or assignment of sublease if there is or has been a breach by the lessee of any of the conditions under the head lease unless proof is produced to the Tribunal that the breach has been made good. 

 [Regulation 28: inserted, on 14 October 2005, by regulation 5 of the Leases Restrictions (Amendment) Regulations 2006 (SN 2006/2) .]

LEASES RESTRICTIONS REGULATIONS 1977 

 PART 2  CRITERIA TO BE APPLIED BY TRIBUNAL 

 29  

 Approval of mortgage 

 The Tribunal may approve the mortgage over any leasehold land if the Tribunal is satisfied that— 

 (a) 

 the mortgagor understands the nature and extent of the mortgage transaction and in the case of a mortgagor who is a Cook Islander the implication of the provisions of the mortgage document have been explained to that mortgagor in the Cook Islands Maori language by an officer of the High Court approved in writing by the Secretary of Justice or the Registrar to be competent for the purpose; and 

 (b) 

 an appropriate certificate duly signed to that effect by the person who carried out the explanation has been endorsed on the document; and 

 (c) 

 the person to whom the explanation in Cook Islands Maori has been given was not held responsible for the cost of providing that explanation but that cost is met by the party or their representative who requires the mortgage document to be recorded in English; and 

 (d) 

 the mortgagor has the ability to fulfill the obligations imposed under the mortgage and that the terms and conditions of the mortgage are not onerous and are fair and reasonable on the mortgagor. 

 [Regulation 29: inserted, on 14 October 2005, by regulation 5 of the Leases Restrictions (Amendment) Regulations 2006 (SN 2006/2) .]

LEASES RESTRICTIONS REGULATIONS 1977 

 PART 2  CRITERIA TO BE APPLIED BY TRIBUNAL 

 30  

 Approval may be refused unless final document executed by parties 

 The Tribunal may not approve any lease or sublease or assignment of lease or assignment of sublease unless the original and final deed or document for the transaction has been duly signed and/or executed by one of the parties thereto and produced to the Tribunal. 

 [Regulation 30: inserted, on 14 October 2005, by section 5 of the Leases Restrictions (Amendment) Regulations 2006 (SN 2006/2) .]

LEASES RESTRICTIONS REGULATIONS 1977 

 PART 2  CRITERIA TO BE APPLIED BY TRIBUNAL 

 31  

 Confirmation by Land Court required 

 No signed or executed lease or sublease or assignment of lease or assignment of sublease pursuant to regulation 30 has any force or effect unless it is confirmed by the Land Court pursuant to section 477 of the Cook Islands Act 1915. 

 [Regulation 31: inserted, on 14 October 2005, by regulation 5 of the Leases Restrictions (Amendment) Regulations 2006 (SN 2006/2) .]

LEASES RESTRICTIONS REGULATIONS 1977 

 PART 2  CRITERIA TO BE APPLIED BY TRIBUNAL 

 32  

 Approval to be granted pursuant to Registrar’s sale 

 The Tribunal must approve the assignment of any lease if such assignment is being made pursuant to a Registrar’s sale and providing such assignment complies with the Leases Restrictions Act 1976 and the Leases Restrictions Regulations 1977. 

 [Regulation 32: inserted, on 14 October 2005, by regulation 5 of the Leases Restrictions (Amendment) Regulations 2006 (SN 2006/2) .]

LEASES RESTRICTIONS REGULATIONS 1977 

 PART 2  CRITERIA TO BE APPLIED BY TRIBUNAL 

 33  

 No approval for assignment or sublease before 10 years of term of lease 

 The Tribunal must not approve any sublease or assignment of any lease unless 10 years from the date of commencement of the lease or sublease has expired except that the Tribunal may approve any sublease or assignment of any lease before the expiry of 10 years from the date of commencement of the lease or sublease when— 

 (a) 

 the consent of the owners residing on the island on which the land is located and to which the application relates has been given; or 

 (b) 

 the Tribunal is satisfied that there are sufficient reasons for such approval to be given. 

 [Regulation 33: inserted, on 14 October 2005, by regulation 5 of the Leases Restrictions (Amendment) Regulations 2006 (SN 2006/2) .]

LEASES RESTRICTIONS REGULATIONS 1977 

 PART 2  CRITERIA TO BE APPLIED BY TRIBUNAL 

 34  

 Right of person to be heard 

 Any person who has any interest in the land that is the subject matter of the application before the Tribunal may, upon verbal or written application being made to the Tribunal, be heard by the Tribunal in respect of the application, and the Tribunal may, after hearing such person and the parties to the application, either adjourn the application upon such conditions as the Tribunal may decide to impose or dismiss the application. 

 [Regulation 34: inserted, on 14 October 2005, by regulation 5 of the Leases Restrictions (Amendment) Regulations 2006 (SN 2006/2) .]

LEASES RESTRICTIONS REGULATIONS 1977 

 PART 2  CRITERIA TO BE APPLIED BY TRIBUNAL 

 35  

 Tribunal may request further information 

 In giving effect to any of the provisions of these regulations, the Tribunal may direct the applicant to produce to the Tribunal such information as may be necessary to enable the Tribunal to make a final decision. 

 [Regulation 35: inserted, on 14 October 2005, by regulation 5 of the Leases Restrictions (Amendment) Regulations 2006 (SN 2006/2) .]

LEASES RESTRICTIONS REGULATIONS 1977 

 PART 2  CRITERIA TO BE APPLIED BY TRIBUNAL 

 36  

 Tribunal may hold sittings in any of islands of Cook Islands 

 The Tribunal may hold sittings in any island of the Cook Islands where the lands affected by the applications before the Tribunal are situated. 

 [Regulation 36: inserted, on14 October 2005, by regulation 5 of the Leases Restrictions (Amendment) Regulations 2006 (SN 2006/2) .]

LEASES RESTRICTIONS REGULATIONS 1977 

 PART 2  CRITERIA TO BE APPLIED BY TRIBUNAL 

 37  

 Approval pursuant to Unit Titles Act 2005 

 Where an application has been made for the approval of the Tribunal in relation to a lease or sublease or assignment of lease or assignment of sublease under the Unit Titles Act 2005, the Tribunal must apply the criteria set out in these regulations and in paragraphs (a) to (f) of this regulation— 

 (a) 

 the owners in the land understand the nature and extent of the development; and 

 (b) 

 the terms of the lease have been complied with; and 

 (c) 

 the lease expressly states the development is pursuant to the Unit Titles Act 2005; and 

 (d) 

 existing traditional easements across the land have been clearly marked on a unit plan pursuant to the Unit Titles Act 2005; and 

 (e) 

 the common property has been clearly marked on any plan and in relation to common property which is vacant land, the intended use of that vacant land has been properly recorded; and 

 (f) 

 the provisions of the Cook Islands Act 1915 have been complied with; and 

 (g) 

 the provisions of section 106A of the Property Law Act 1952 as it applies in the Cook Islands have been complied with. 

 [Regulation 37: inserted, on 14 October 2005, by regulation 5 of the Leases Restrictions (Amendment) Regulations 2006 (SN 2006/2) .]

LEASES RESTRICTIONS REGULATIONS 1977 

 PART 2  CRITERIA TO BE APPLIED BY TRIBUNAL 

 38  

 No right of renewal 

 The Tribunal must not approve any lease, sublease, assignment of lease or assignment of sublease in which there is a clause giving the lessee or sub-lessee as the case may be a right to renew the term of the lease, unless the owners in the land have considered that clause and the Tribunal is satisfied that: 

 (a) 

 the nature and extent of the clause has been explained to those owners in the land in the Cook Islands Maori language by an officer of the High Court approved in writing by the Secretary of Justice or the Registrar to be competent for the purpose; and 

 (b) 

 an appropriate certificate duly signed to that effect by the person who carried out the explanation has been endorsed on the document; and 

 (c) 

 the person or persons to whom the explanation in Cook Islands Maori has been given was not held responsible for the cost of providing that explanation but that cost is met by the party or their representative who requires the clause to be recorded in English. 

 [Regulation 38: inserted, on 14 October 2005, by regulation 5 of the Leases Restrictions (Amendment) Regulations 2006 (SN 2006/2) .]

LEASES RESTRICTIONS REGULATIONS 1977 

 PART 2  CRITERIA TO BE APPLIED BY TRIBUNAL 

 39  

 Removal of improvements at expiry of lease 

 The Tribunal must not approve any lease, sublease, assignment of lease or assignment of sublease in which there is a clause giving the lessee the right to remove improvements to the land at the expiry of the lease unless those improvements are stated in the clause to be chattels or tenants fixtures in accordance with the common law and the owners in the land have considered that clause and the Tribunal is satisfied that: 

 (a) 

 the nature and extent of the clause has been explained to those owners in the land in the Cook Islands Maori language by an officer of the High Court approved in writing by the Secretary of Justice or the Registrar to be competent for the purpose; and 

 (b) 

 an appropriate certificate duly signed to that effect by the person who carried out the explanation has been endorsed on the document; and 

 (c) 

 the person or persons to whom the explanation in Cook Islands Maori has been given was not held responsible for the cost of providing that explanation but that cost is met by the party or their representative who requires the clause to be recorded in English. 

 [Regulation 39: inserted, on 14 October 2005, by regulation 5 of the Leases Restrictions (Amendment) Regulations 2006 (SN 2006/2) .]

LEASES RESTRICTIONS REGULATIONS 1977 

 PART 2  CRITERIA TO BE APPLIED BY TRIBUNAL 

 40  

 Improvements to be left in good state of repair 

 The Tribunal must not approve any lease, sublease, assignment of lease or assignment of sublease unless there is a clause requiring that at the expiry of the lease or sublease the lessee must repair and make good at its own expense any damage which may be done to the land and must leave at its own expense any improvements in a good state of repair. 

 [Regulation 40: inserted, on 14 October 2005, by regulation 5 of the Leases Restrictions (Amendment) Regulations 2006 (SN 2006/2) .]
